2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 as constituted Attorney by the opposite party No.2 being plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit No.367 of 2001 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the judgment and sole decree dated 06.11.2000 obtained by the defendants in Title Suit No.278 of 2000 is fraudulent collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia that the plaintiff No.1 came to know about the disputed sole decree of Title Suit No.278 of 2000 on 05.08.2001 for the first time. In fact the plaintiffs did not engage any lawyer to conduct the suit nor signed any `solenama' and the defendant. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the Courts below during passing the orders committed illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned trial Court in rejecting the applications filed under Order 7 Rule 11 and Order 11 Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure committed illegality inasmuch as the pleadings of the plaintiffs is not correct rather it is false and fabricated. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendants do not admit the signature of the plaintiffs in their passports but the learned Court below allowing the application of the plaintiffs sent the passport for Expert's opinion to compare the signatures of the plaintiffs with the solenama and the signature of the plaintiffs in Title Suit No.278 of 2000. Admittedly, the present plaintiffs-opposite parties were alive at the time of institution of the suit on 07.10.2001 and the signature of Danish Ali can easily be obtained in the Court but after 10 (ten) years the learned Court sent the passport which is disputed; to the hand writing Expert and as such in sending the passport to the Expert for his opinion is illegal. The learned Courts below failed to consider the settled principle of law which is very much clear in several decisions of this Court and our Apex Court that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get a decree for simple declaration that the sole decree is fraudulent and illegal. More so, the rejection of the plaint in appropriate case can be done under the inherent power of the Court under Section 151 of the Code of, civil Procedure. The learned Advocate in support of his submission referred several decisions of this Court and our. Apex Court and lastly submits that in passing the impugned judgment and order there has been miscarriage of justice and the impugned order was passed on non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice which deserve interference of this Court. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate of the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the learned Advocate of the petitioners and submits that both the trial Court as well as the Revisional Court during passing their orders committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that in the original plaint there is a clear allegation from the side of the plaintiffs that the solenama' was Obtained by false personification and the signature of the plaintiff in the vokalatnama and in the deposition of the plaintiff No.1 before the Court is false. The learned Advocate also submits that in paragraph No.4. 5 and 6 of the plaint the specific contention of the plaintiffs is such that they have challenged their signatures in the solenama, vokalatnama and in the  deposition. From the averment of the plaint it is clear that there exist specific cause of action which require adjudication into the matter-in-dispute and before taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties the matter-in-controversy can not be adjudicated. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the subject matter of the plaint ease is a mater of evidence and both the Courts below correctly held that at this stage the plaint can not be rejected before trial. As to the correctness of the allegation; evidence is required. More so, the grounds of the application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure are not proper for rejection of the plaint. The learned Advocate in support of his argument referred several decisions of this Court and our Apex Court and lastly submits that in rejecting the application filed under Order 7 Rule I I & Order II Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure no illegality or irregularity was done by the Courts below and there is no non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and order can be interfered with. 

 10. On perusal of the Civil Revision case record along with the connected papers it appears that the plaintiffs to the suit filed the original suit for declaration that the sole decree passed in Title Suit No.278 of 2000 dated 06.11.2000 and 22.11.2000 respectively is false, collusive and fraudulent and in their plaint paragraph No.4 is their cause of action. The case of the plaintiff's as it appears in paragraph NO.5 and 6 is such that in Title Suit No.278 of 2000 before the 10 Court of learned the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka they never engaged any lawyer on their behalf and never put any signature in the vokalatnama. They also did not prove their signature in the solenama. The defendant No.1 to that suit who is the plaintiff No.1 of the original Suit No.367 of 2001 Akram Ali as D.W.1 neither gave any deposition before the learned Court nor gave his signature therein and all the signatures as it appears in the papers are fabricated and created by false personification.
